issues.claim: V04's round-4 trigger names 'the frame growth's deck extension' among the epoch changes to a raised way (V04 §3.5.0 *At an epoch*, l. 1340–1343; §3.10, l. 2286–2289; §1b.2; T-V4-63), and V04 §3.5.0 keeps 'An epoch op removes no obstacle … so the element set it collapses is the one a regeneration of the same state collapses (T-V4-65; V06's T-V6-67)', `Foundations.apply` being collapse-only. Whether the extension keeps the old deck's stations is stated nowhere. §3.2 (9) (base l. 3667) and `RaisedFoot` (l. 2313–2317) say only 'the raised way's re-derivation then extends the deck to the new ring … as §4.11 continues a through-road'. The support step that re-derivation runs spaces the n − 1 interior stations evenly at L ÷ n over the whole deck ((2), l. 2534) and, for a changed course, keeps only the KEY of a station within p ÷ 2 of a former one ((5), l. 2572), so as L grows every old pier may move by up to p ÷ 2. Support step (6) (b) (l. 2596–2598) holds a standing raised way ('nothing laid later … moves, adds or omits a station') but lists 'a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)' among the ops that change it without saying how. T110-2's frame-growth clause tests only the foot's ends. One builder re-spaces the whole deck: old footings leave, V04's collapse-only `Foundations.apply` keeps elements `collapsed` and pillars standing under no pier (unequal to a regeneration, so T-V4-65's at-epoch bar fails), and a re-sited pier can land on a building raised since generation (plots and footprints are no obstacle of (3); S8 holed them round the old rings), against (6) (b)'s held reservation. Another builder keeps the old stations and lays stations on the extension only. The V04 repair left this as a hand-off ('the base's text decides'); the base's text does not decide it. Graded MAJOR: two builders, two behaviours, off the common path; the re-spacing reading's pier-in-a-building outcome would be a blocker's impossible result there.
issues.required_change: Model §2.7's support step (6) (b), after '… a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)), and none drops it.': add 'A frame growth's extension keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` — and every span between them with its `use` and `reason`; (1)–(5) and the span rule run on the extension alone, from the old deck's last interior station to the deck's new end on the new ring, its stations' keys minted after the largest the way has held ((5)); so no pier of the old deck moves and no footing leaves (V04 §3.5.0 *At an epoch*).' The `RaisedFoot` comment's 'then extends the deck to the new ring as §4.11 continues a through-road' adds '(the old deck's stations kept, the support step's (6) (b))'. Ends: scope §13.2's T110-2 frame-growth clause adds 'every station of the old deck at its key, position and ring after the growth'; V04 T-V4-65's at-epoch clause adds 'and an aqueduct whose deck a frame growth extends over a cavern chamber within reach of its piers: no old pier moved, the collapsed set equal to a regeneration's'.
